findings.description: Content Security Policy allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' for script-src, and 'unsafe-inline' for style-src. This significantly weakens XSS protection as inline scripts and eval() are permitted.
findings.remediation: Remove 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' from script-src. Use nonces or hashes for inline scripts. Move inline styles to external CSS files. If inline scripts are required for Tauri's IPC, use 'nonce-<random>' pattern with a CSP nonce generated per request.

findings.description: connect-src allows all localhost ports (http://localhost:*, ws://localhost:*, http://127.0.0.1:*) which is overly permissive. An attacker who compromises a local service could exfiltrate data.
findings.current_value: connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost http://localhost:* ws://localhost:* ws://127.0.0.1:* http://127.0.0.1:*
findings.remediation: Restrict connect-src to only the specific ports used: http://localhost:8080 http://localhost:8081 ws://localhost:8080 ws://localhost:8081. Remove wildcard port allowances.

findings.description: The 'main-window' capability grants 'core:default' and 'opener:default' permissions. 'core:default' includes many powerful APIs (window management, clipboard, etc.). No principle of least privilege applied.
findings.remediation: Define explicit, minimal permissions. Replace 'core:default' with specific permissions needed: 'core:window:default', 'core:event:default', etc. Use 'core:webview:default' if webview APIs are needed. Avoid 'core:default' in production.

findings.description: DevTools not explicitly disabled in release build. Tauri 2 enables DevTools in debug builds only by default, but explicit configuration is recommended for defense-in-depth.
findings.remediation: Add "devtools": false to the window configuration or ensure Tauri's default behavior (DevTools only in debug) is preserved. Consider adding to tauri.conf.json: "windows": [{"security": {"devtools": false}}] for explicit release hardening.

findings.description: RTMP server default bind_address is '127.0.0.1' (localhost only). This is GOOD - not binding to 0.0.0.0. However, the setting is user-configurable via Settings.bind_address and could be changed to 0.0.0.0.
findings.remediation: Add validation in SettingsManager::save() or update_settings command to reject 0.0.0.0 or non-loopback addresses for bind_address. Log a warning if non-localhost binding is attempted.

findings.description: Web UI server (port 8081) and Overlay server (port 8080) both bind to 127.0.0.1 only. This is GOOD - not exposed to network.
findings.remediation: No action needed. Configuration is secure by default.

findings.description: CORS configured with allow_origin(Any), allow_methods(Any), allow_headers(Any) on both main API and overlay routers. This allows any origin to make requests to the local servers.
findings.remediation: Restrict CORS to specific origins. For local-only servers, use allow_origin("http://localhost:8080").allow_origin("http://localhost:8081").allow_origin("tauri://localhost").allow_origin("https://tauri.localhost") or implement origin validation middleware that only allows Tauri's custom protocol origins.

findings.description: Multiple plugins loaded with default permissions: shell, dialog, opener, http, notification, global-shortcut. No capability restrictions defined for these plugins in tauri.conf.json.
findings.remediation: Define explicit capabilities for each plugin in tauri.conf.json. For example, shell should only allow specific commands if needed. http should restrict to specific domains. global-shortcut should be scoped to registered hotkeys only.

findings.description: No tauri-plugin-updater dependency found. Auto-updates not configured. This is acceptable if updates are handled externally, but should be documented.
findings.remediation: If auto-updates are desired, add tauri-plugin-updater with proper signature verification configuration. If not desired, document the update strategy in README.

findings.description: Settings stored in user config directory via tauri-plugin-store. No file system scope restrictions defined in capabilities. Settings include sensitive data (stream keys, auth tokens).
findings.remediation: Define explicit file system scope in capabilities to restrict access to only the settings file. Consider encrypting sensitive settings (stream keys, web_ui_auth_token) at rest.

findings.description: Web UI has optional auth_token setting (web_ui_auth_token) but it's not enforced on API endpoints. The auth_token is stored in state but no middleware validates it on incoming requests.
findings.current_value: auth_token: Option<String> in WebServerState, not used in route handlers
findings.remediation: Implement authentication middleware for /api/* routes when web_ui_auth_token is set. Validate token via Authorization header or query parameter. Return 401 for unauthorized requests.

findings.description: Overlay served on localhost:8080 for OBS browser source. Main window runs on different port (dev: 1420, prod: tauri://localhost). Cross-origin but same host. No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors headers set on overlay responses.
findings.current_value: No frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options headers on overlay routes
findings.remediation: Add CSP frame-ancestors directive to overlay responses: frame-ancestors 'self' http://localhost:8080 http://localhost:8081 tauri://localhost. Or use X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (though CSP is preferred).

findings.description: withGlobalTauri: true exposes __TAURI__ global on window object. This allows any JavaScript in the webview to access Tauri APIs. Combined with weak CSP, this increases attack surface.
findings.remediation: Set withGlobalTauri: false and use Tauri's context isolation (invoke via IPC only). If global access is needed for specific APIs, use a custom preload script to expose only required functions.

findings.description: freezePrototype: false allows JavaScript prototype modifications. Could lead to prototype pollution attacks if untrusted code executes.
findings.remediation: Set freezePrototype: true to prevent prototype pollution. Test for compatibility as this may break some libraries.

findings.description: Custom protocol feature available but not enabled (custom-protocol = ["tauri/custom-protocol"]). No custom protocols registered in tauri.conf.json.
findings.remediation: No action needed. Feature is opt-in and not enabled.
